mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand offset by a nascent housing recovery, resulting in flat to mildly positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
regime_hint: late-cycle demand softening with housing stabilization
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately driving higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below -1% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND < -1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance, which immediately raises risk-free rates and equity financing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: immediate reaction to aggressive rate hike
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly for two months) and a surge in retail sales (proxied by RSAFS growth > 1% monthly for two months) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +0.5% AND RSAFS > previous month +1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS monthly change falling from >0.4% to <0% within one month) signals labor market cooling, which reduces wage pressure and supports lower inflation, ultimately producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change drops from >0.4% to <0% within one month
regime_hint: transition from tight to easing labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.4%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months signals a disinflationary environment, which lowers real discount rates and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY change < 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
